body.objective: Build the first fail-closed complex-frequency Evans/connection preflight for upper-half-plane axial Bach modes on Schwarzschild.
body.stop_condition: Starting from the terminal real-frequency global connection package, complexify the exact six-state flow and endpoint recurrences on an explicitly bounded rectangle Re(M omega) in [1/2,3/4], Im(M omega) in [0,eta]. Construct interval or ball enclosures of the horizon-decaying and infinity-admissible subbundles away from thresholds, define a basis-invariant Evans determinant or exterior-product section, and prove analyticity plus nonvanishing basis normalizations. Run an argument-principle or validated contour enclosure that either counts all zeros in the rectangle or certifies the first exact obstruction to doing so. Separate physical upper-half-plane poles from gauge, endpoint-basis and exceptional-wall zeros. Include independent replay and mutations that reverse the temporal convention, omit a generalized/logarithmic endpoint column, cross an unresolved threshold, or infer zero count from sampled nonzero values.
body.forbid: no real-frequency rank theorem called pole absence; no grid scan called an argument-principle count; no uncontrolled complex shooting; no gauge or endpoint normalization zero called an instability; no bounded rectangle result called full mode stability
body.resource_hint: Treat the first bounded complex-frequency rectangle as a preflight. If the current interval library lacks complex balls, exterior algebra or validated argument-principle support, emit a precise Forge request and freeze the missing theorem rather than sampling.
notes: This is a stability diagnostic, not part of the minimum real-frequency channel verdict.
The sign of Im(omega) must be tied explicitly to the exp(+i omega v) convention.
